findings.title: BaseAgentAdapter.ts grows further past 500 lines
findings.problem: code-quality.md Code Structure Guidelines say files stay under 500 lines; this change adds a net 85 lines, taking the file to 1512 lines.
findings.impact: The documented code-quality standard is moved further out of conformance by this change instead of held or improved.
findings.recommendation: Extract the added signal-forwarding/session-finalization helpers into a separate co-located module and call them from BaseAgentAdapter.

findings.title: Completed save can recreate renamed live record
findings.problem: saveSession checks for the concurrent-rename race after writing only for status 'active'. A 'completed' save that picked {id}.json while another process renamed it to completed_ recreates {id}.json. The after-write rm(livePath) can also delete a new generation's live record written in between.
findings.impact: The start pass treats the recreated {id}.json as undelivered and may deliver it again, or a fresh generation's record can be removed. Reachability unconfirmed: whether every completed save and rename runs under the same reconcile lock was not established.
findings.recommendation: Apply the post-write rename-race check to completed saves too (write to completed_ when the live file vanished meanwhile), and only rm the live path when it is still the copy this call wrote.

findings.title: Exit notice counts other wrappers' drops
findings.problem: countDroppedSince counts every record in the shared sessions folder with droppedAt >= this wrapper's start, including drops made by other concurrent wrappers. The docs scope the notice to drops by this wrapper (its start pass, its exit, its hooks' /clear).
findings.impact: Each running wrapper reports the same drops, and a wrapper reports data loss it did not cause. That undermines the 13765 message meant to tell harmless exits from real loss.
findings.recommendation: Stamp the dropping process (e.g. droppedBy pid/startedAt) on the record and count only drops made by this wrapper, its start pass and its hooks.

findings.title: "Nothing is lost" exit promise can be false
findings.problem: PENDING_EXIT_NOTICE says the analytics 'will be sent at the next codemie start. Nothing is lost.' whenever the own {id}.json has a codemieUrl. Only a start against the same host with a send path delivers it, and after 3 failed attempts the record is dropped.
findings.impact: Users are told nothing is lost in cases where the data is later dropped or never sent. This contradicts the 13765 requirement to tell harmless cancellation apart from data loss.
findings.recommendation: Reword PENDING_EXIT_NOTICE to state the real condition (sent by a later codemie start against the same CodeMie host, up to 3 attempts) and drop the unconditional "Nothing is lost".

findings.title: Kimi records never bounded by later record
findings.problem: sameTranscriptKeys has no case for kimi or kimi-acp, so it returns [] and nextRecordStart is always undefined for kimi records. Kimi --resume runs reuse the same per-session wire.jsonl (getKimiMainWirePath). gap_shape: other. Evidence: the switch covers claude/gemini/codex, -acp variants, copilot-cli, opencode, codemie-code, pi. The nextRecordStart tests cover no kimi case.
findings.impact: Consumer: finalizeSession in hook.ts (recordsBeforeMs = await nextRecordStart(record)). A reconciled stranded kimi record gets no bound, so the flush and lastRecordAt take in a later resumed run's records. That inflates the stranded session's end time and metrics.
findings.recommendation: Add `case 'kimi': case 'kimi-acp':` keyed on correlation.agentSessionFile (normalized to `kimi:`), and a nextRecordStart test bounding a stranded kimi record by a later one over the same wire.jsonl.

findings.title: Other profiles' records sent with this launch's credentials
findings.problem: The start pass delivers other sessions' stranded/undelivered records with this launch's SSO cookies and send path. The only filter is sameHost (host string equality), and recordHookConfig stamps this launch's CODEMIE_PROFILE_NAME. Nothing compares profile or analytics identity.
findings.impact: A record written under another profile or CodeMie account on the same host is delivered and attributed under the current launch's credentials, which corrupts per-user analytics. Reachability unconfirmed: whether two accounts on one host share a sessions folder in practice was not established.
findings.recommendation: Store the owning profile (or analytics identity) on the record and deliver only when it matches this launch; otherwise finalize locally or leave queued.

findings.title: Attempt counter spent when no send ran
findings.problem: attemptRecord persists the attempt bump in beginAttempt, and rollBackAttempt runs only on the non-throwing path when stopped(). An attempt that throws after the abort/deadline, or a launch that exits while the start pass is in a sync parse or ps call longer than ABANDON_WAIT_MS, keeps the bump without any send.
findings.impact: A few short launches can use up MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a stranded record is finalized without its flush, or an undelivered one is dropped unsent. Reachability unconfirmed: whether deliverSession/finalizeRecord can throw past their own catches was not traced.
findings.recommendation: Roll the attempt back in a finally when stopped(), and persist the counter bump only once a send was actually attempted, so an abandoned or throwing attempt never burns MAX_ATTEMPTS.

findings.title: Records dropped unsent after three attempts
findings.problem: EPMCDME-16539 Expected Result asks that undelivered lines be retried until delivered, or files renamed only after delivery is confirmed. After MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 the record is renamed completed_ without being delivered and gets droppedAt; the test asserts endMetricSentAt undefined on the renamed record. The Jira comment and PR call this intended, but the ticket text was never changed.
findings.impact: Analytics lines the server keeps rejecting are lost permanently. That is a partial on a required spec requirement, and it does not match either option in the ticket.
findings.recommendation: Decide with the ticket owner: either update EPMCDME-16539's Expected Result to accept a bounded 3-attempt drop (with the dropped-analytics notice), or keep the record queued until delivery is confirmed.

findings.title: Codex/Copilot transcript lookup scans unbounded history
findings.problem: Codex window mode in findRolloutForRun sets maxAgeDays from Date.now() - run.startedAt with no limit, so a months-old stranded record discovers and parses every rollout over months in the wrapper process. Copilot locateTranscript also synchronously reads every events.jsonl modified since the record's start.
findings.impact: A wrapper start can stall on synchronous I/O that the start-pass deadline cannot abort, which delays the agent launch. Reachability unconfirmed: how old stranded codex/copilot records get in practice was not established.
findings.recommendation: Bound the window-mode discovery (limit and/or an upper time bound via nextRecordStartInDirectory) and make Copilot locateTranscript reads async and capped, so an old stranded record cannot stall the wrapper start.

findings.title: Kimi lastRecordAt has no test
findings.problem: Kimi's new lastRecordAt (recordTimes from event.time, bounded by recordsBeforeMs) sets the end time of a stranded kimi/kimi-acp record's synthetic SessionEnd, but no test checks it. gap_shape: regression-gap. Evidence: last-record-at.test.ts covers claude, codex, pi, copilot-cli and gemini only, and the kimi tests only cover the hook transformer's pass-through.
findings.impact: Consumer: finalizeSession in hook.ts, which reads lastRecordAt for the synthetic end. If kimi stops returning it or maps the wrong field, the end time silently falls back to lastDeltaAt/startTime and the stranded kimi session's duration is wrong. No current test would fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a kimi case to src/agents/core/session/__tests__/last-record-at.test.ts: a wire.jsonl with events at T1/T2/T3 (epoch ms); assert lastRecordAt === T3 unbounded and === T2 with recordsBeforeMs = T3.

findings.title: OpenCode storage path may resolve wrong storage
findings.problem: USER_XDG_DATA_HOME is captured when opencode.paths.ts first loads, so if the module loads after a codemie-code launch pointed XDG_DATA_HOME at its private storage, opencode records are searched in the wrong storage. getAgentOpenCodeStoragePath ignores a user's OPENCODE_STORAGE_PATH override. codemie-code onSessionEnd no longer sets OPENCODE_STORAGE_PATH and passes the storage path only to discoverSessions, so downstream parsing / getOpenCodeDbPath may resolve the user's storage.
findings.impact: OpenCode or codemie-code sessions can be finalized over the wrong storage, producing missing or wrong analytics for the built-in agent. Reachability unconfirmed: module load order and the downstream path resolution were not traced.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the user XDG data home lazily (or capture it before any codemie-code override), honour OPENCODE_STORAGE_PATH for opencode records, and pass codemie-code's private storage explicitly through processEvent/adapter parsing instead of relying on the removed env override.

findings.title: OpenCode locateTranscript picks newest session unbounded
findings.problem: locateTranscript takes the newest discovered session (maxAgeDays: 1; no cwd filter for codemie-code, limit 1 for opencode) with no lower bound at the record's start and no upper bound at the next record's start, unlike the codex and copilot implementations that use nextRecordStartInDirectory.
findings.impact: A stranded opencode/codemie-code record can be flushed over a later run's (or the current launch's) transcript, which attributes another session's data to it. Records older than a day find nothing and lose their flush.
findings.recommendation: Filter discovered sessions to created >= record.startTime and < nextRecordStartInDirectory(record), add the cwd filter for codemie-code, and drop the 1-day maxAgeDays cap for stranded records.

findings.title: 'Hook cancelled' still seen on normal exit
findings.problem: EPMCDME-13765 AC: the SessionEnd CodeMie hook no longer produces 'Hook cancelled' during normal codemie-claude exit. The mechanism is in place (local-only finalize when the wrapper is alive on prompt_input_exit/logout, liveWrapperDelivering), but the author's own live evidence shows 1 of 30 normal exits still printing the message, with the cause not reproduced.
findings.impact: A required story criterion is only partly met. Users can still see the cancellation error this ticket exists to remove.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the residual 1-in-30 'Hook cancelled' on normal codemie-claude exit is acceptable for EPMCDME-13765; if not, find the remaining slow path in the SessionEnd hook before closing the ticket.

findings.title: Stranded flush not bounded by next record
findings.problem: performIncrementalSync sets context.recordsBeforeMs, but the adapters use it only to compute lastRecordAt (e.g. claude.session.ts latestRecordTime). The processors still run over every message in the transcript, including lines a later record over the same transcript (e.g. a resumed claude transcript) also covers.
findings.impact: The later session's lines can be counted under both the stranded record and its own record, which double-counts analytics. Reachability unconfirmed: whether server-side dedupe by line id absorbs the duplicate was not established.
findings.recommendation: Filter parsed transcript messages to records with time < context.recordsBeforeMs before running processors, not only when computing lastRecordAt.

findings.title: Same-generation rename overwrites completed files
findings.problem: For the same generation, renameSessionFiles renames the live metrics/conversation files over the existing completed_ ones. Lines that exist only in the older completed files are lost locally, as the inline ponytail comment admits.
findings.impact: codemie analytics reads the completed_ files, so local reports lose those lines. Reachability unconfirmed: when a same-generation live set reappears next to its completed_ set was not traced.
findings.recommendation: For the same generation, append/merge the live metrics and conversation JSONL into the existing completed_ files instead of renaming over them, so codemie analytics keeps every line.

findings.title: /clear lock timeout merges generations
findings.problem: When /clear's SessionStart cannot take the reconcile lock in time, closeClearedGeneration logs and returns, and handleSessionStart still calls createSessionRecord, which reuses the live previous record as a re-entered session.
findings.impact: The cleared and new generations merge into one record, or an undelivered completed {id}.json is overwritten. Reachability unconfirmed: createSessionRecord's handling of a completed {id}.json was not read.
findings.recommendation: When the reconcile lock is not taken, still keep the fresh generation apart (move the previous set aside, or skip reusing the previous record in createSessionRecord) rather than proceeding as if it were closed.

findings.title: no-send-path skip loses end metric permanently
findings.problem: sendSessionEndMetrics persists endMetricSkipped 'no-send-path' (and 'no-analytics-config') when this launch has CODEMIE_URL but no send path, e.g. the proxy is not started. isDeliveryDone treats a skipped metric as done, so the record is renamed completed_. finalizeOwnRecord's active branch also processes with deliver:true without the hasSendPath check its completed branch has.
findings.impact: The end metric is never sent, even by a later start that does have a send path. This contradicts the 'file name is the queue / delivered by a later start' model this change introduces.
findings.recommendation: Do not persist endMetricSkipped for 'no-send-path' (and missing analytics config when CODEMIE_URL is set later): leave the record undelivered as {id}.json so a later start with a send path delivers it; and gate finalizeOwnRecord's active branch on hasSendPath like the completed branch.

findings.title: hook.ts grows further past 500 lines
findings.problem: code-quality.md Code Structure Guidelines say files stay under 500 lines with one main export per file; this change adds a net 426 lines to an already oversized file, taking it from 1659 to 2085 lines.
findings.impact: The documented code-quality standard is moved further out of conformance by this change instead of held or improved.
findings.recommendation: Move the new session-delivery/finalization logic added to hook.ts into its own module(s) under src/agents/core/session/ or src/cli/commands/hook/ and import it from hook.ts.

findings.title: Sync lock no longer reclaimed by age
findings.problem: isSyncLockStale used to reclaim the lock by age (120 s). A lock that names a pid is now stale only when the holder is dead. A bare-pid lock from an older CLI version, or any holder checked pidOnly in hook processes, whose pid has been reused by a long-lived unrelated process is never reclaimed.
findings.impact: That session's sync is blocked indefinitely. Reachability unconfirmed: how often legacy bare-pid locks survive an upgrade was not established.
findings.recommendation: Keep an age ceiling (SYNC_LOCK_STALE_MS) as a fallback for holders without startedAt (bare-pid legacy locks and pidOnly checks), so a reused pid cannot block the session's sync forever.

findings.title: EPERM-alive breaks daemon liveness callers
findings.problem: isProcessAlive used to treat any error as dead and now treats EPERM as alive. This shared helper is also used by daemon-manager checkStatus/start/stop and by connect-orchestrator ensureOtlpProxy; only stopDaemon was adjusted.
findings.impact: A stale proxy daemon state whose pid now belongs to another user's process reads as running. checkStatus reports the daemon up and ensureOtlpProxy skips the respawn, so OTLP hook forwarding targets a dead proxy.
findings.recommendation: Keep isProcessAlive's EPERM semantics for locks if needed, but have daemon-manager checkStatus and connect-orchestrator ensureOtlpProxy use isOwnerAlive({pid, startedAt}) or a health probe so a pid reused by another user's process is not taken for the running daemon.
